content: libclang exposes a stable plain C ABI over the C++ Clang codebase specifically to isolate callers from C++ exception propagation and C++ ABI instability -- exceptions are caught at the C API boundary and converted to error codes/sentinel values before crossing. This is the direct precedent for mediadiff's 'libmediadiff has no stdout and no exit(), no exceptions cross the boundary' rule, though mediadiff's boundary is C++/C++ (lib to CLI) not C++/C, so the isolation is about exception-safety and control-flow discipline rather than ABI stability -- still the same principle: catch everything at the outermost internal boundary, translate to Error, never let an exception unwind past the library edge.
